# Install, config and test-runner detection

- Tracker r34 #362 — `REQ-R34-CLOSURE-001`: direct local `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` must reach the real TDD runner within a 15-second observation budget on the representative installed TypeScript 5.9.3 fixture. Discovery must preserve full launcher/bundle bytes, literal helper dependencies, and package-resolution metadata, or explicitly refuse before writing evidence. `timeoutMs` remains the runner timeout, not a discovery timeout.
  PASS/counterexamples (defined before implementation): `TEST-R34-CLOSURE-001` limits filesystem reads/stat probes to 1,000 for a multi-MiB source with 150 distinct identifiers shared by two checks (counterexample: per-token PATH probing); `TEST-R34-CLOSURE-002` requires real assertion Red, Green, rejected bundle/helper/metadata drift and restored positives within 15 seconds per invocation (counterexamples: preflight timeout, omitted installed inputs, accepted passing Red); `TEST-R34-CLOSURE-003` requires an explicit bounded-discovery refusal and unchanged ledger for oversized definitions (counterexample: truncating and accepting unknown inputs). Timing is a generous feasibility observation, not a machine-independent latency guarantee.
  Discovery budgets apply per closure: 16 MiB per definition, 64 MiB cumulative text, 2,000,000 lexical tokens, 8,000,000 inspection steps (including command suffix scans), 16 nested quoted fragments, 128 nested definition files, 4,096 directory probes, 200,000 directory entries, and 200,000 unique path/executable/contextual candidates. Existing regular inputs that cannot be read also refuse explicitly. These are structural work bounds, not wall-clock guarantees for filesystem/OS stalls. Resolution, tokenization and negative lookups are cached within one closure; new command boundaries rediscover and hash inputs, so added dependencies and changed bytes remain protected. Nothing exempts `node_modules`. `TEST-R34-CLOSURE-004` exercises token, suffix-work and directory exhaustion with unchanged evidence. Run the real compiler regression with `SDD_R34_TYPESCRIPT=/path/to/typescript` pointing to an existing official 5.9.3 installation; the default uses the Wave 24 repro installation. The test copies it into its repository-local fixture and installs nothing.
  Verification: `node --test --test-name-pattern='r34f #362' <skill>/scripts/sdd.test.mjs` passes all four regressions. Against `dcbedc8`, structural discovery asserts Red at 1,001 probes and oversized input wrongly records Red (assertion failure, not timeout evidence). On Node 24.21.0, the 6,100,000-byte shared structural fixture uses 102 reads/stats; the 6,213,122-byte real compiler fixture completes Red in 5,697.0 ms, Green in 8,443.6 ms and a valid gate in 8,982.2 ms. Bundle/helper/package-metadata mutations reject, then byte-restored controls pass; passing native assertions cannot establish Red. Seven isolated implementation mutations (per-token PATH probing; removal of byte, token, suffix-work or directory limits; dropping bundle or metadata hashes) each fail the corresponding regression by assertion, and restored source passes. Both scripts pass `node --check`; 36 targeted pre-existing closure/provenance controls pass. No full-suite claim is made.

- Tracker r32 (#348, #352): check-definition snapshots include Cargo workspace/package manifests, feature/target admission, default/custom build scripts and local build helpers; TypeScript checks include the selected/default tsconfig, JSONC `extends` chains (including package configs), and project references. Definition drift retains strict/warn policy. Cargo test gates also require every annotated Rust test in the checked surface to appear as executed, regardless of scope policy; direct commands request JSON artifact messages to distinguish same-named targets. Wrappers must preserve observable test output (and JSON artifact messages for ambiguous targets); quiet/hidden, ignored or zero-execution results cannot prove coverage.
- Tracker r32 (#349–#351): check provenance fingerprints PATH-selected executables and symlink targets, including ignored launchers (compared with Green rather than Git absence). The definition closure includes `.npmrc`, protected npm lifecycle wrappers, explicit `make -f`/`--file` inputs and local pytest plugins. Direct pytest runs use isolated, hook-free Python startup with explicit package directories; execution reports reject collection-only checks, missing annotated test identities and plugin-forged successful exit codes. Review definition changes and re-record with `tdd refactor`.

- Install per-user (`~/.copilot/skills/lean-sdd-tdd`) when the target repo asserts its skill list (e.g. a test enumerating `.github/skills`); copying into `.github/skills` can break such tests. Run `node <skill>/scripts/sdd.mjs --root <repo> ...`.
- Build the target first (`npm run build`) if its CLI tests need build artifacts, before `gate`.
- `.sdd/config.json`: `scan:{include:[],exclude:["fixtures/**"]}` (globs; only comment-leading `@id` lines count; in Python, a line that starts a triple-quoted docstring or sits inside one also counts); `timeoutMs` globally or per check; check `changedCmd` with `{changedFiles}`/`{changedTests}` used by `gate --changed` (auto: `vitest related`, `jest --findRelatedTests`). `gate --changed` uses `changedTimeoutMs` (default 60s) so hub-file changes fail fast with `TIMEOUT`; narrow with `changedCmd` such as `["npx","vitest","run","{changedTests}","{changedScopes}"]` (scopes = package dirs). Always run the full `gate` (no `--changed`) before merge. Non-JS stacks get an auto `changedCmd` (no-pkg roots): Go `{changedGoPkgs}` (changed packages + reverse deps via `go list`), Rust `{changedCargoPkgs}` (`-p` changed crates + dependents via `cargo metadata`), Maven `{changedModulesCsv}` (changed modules + dependents + every upstream module they need, from the poms, so diamond dependencies resolve without `-am -amd`; falls back to the full run if the poms cannot be read), Go scoping also works in a repo without commits, Gradle `{changedGradleTasks}` (`:mod:cleanTest :mod:test` for changed modules plus dependents found from `project(':x')` references; not `buildDependents`, which misses later-evaluated dependents), CMake `{changedCtestRegex}` (`ctest -R` of changed test files). When a change cannot be scoped (go.mod/Cargo.*/root Gradle files, non-test C/C++ sources, CMake files, files outside any module) the full check runs and `! cmd …: cannot scope changes` is printed (for Rust: `cannot scope changes for the changed Cargo packages`). A `conftest.py` that defines only non-autouse fixtures the test never names (and no `pytest_*` hooks) is not an oracle of that test. `gate --changed` also scopes in tests whose recorded oracle files (e.g. a contract) changed. `impact` is file-granular (a note says so); the `tdd green` shared-implementation warning is per-`@implements`-block (ledger field `implBlocks`, #287; falls back to the whole file when the block cannot be delimited, and to file mtime for older ledger entries without the field). Hub detection (JS/TS relative-import graph): if > `hubThreshold` (0.25) of test files depend on the change, `hubFallbackCmd` runs (`{changedTests} {directTests}`); if that exceeds `hubMaxTests` (30) the check is skipped as INCOMPLETE instead of timing out. Workspace package names and tsconfig `paths` are followed. For hub changes the uncommitted diff is mapped to exported symbols (comment/whitespace-only ⇒ skipped; declarations mentioning the symbol are tainted transitively) so only tests that can reach them run; unknown diffs (non-exported/top-level code, `export *`) keep the whole hub set; an empty selection is INCOMPLETE, never an unscoped full run. Timeouts report `TIMEOUT`, not FAIL.
- `flaky: {retries?: 1, policy?: "fail"|"warn"}` (#303): a failed `test` check is re-run `retries` times (0 disables). A pass on re-run prints `cmd test FLAKY suspected …`: `fail` (default) keeps the gate FAIL, `warn` accepts it with the warning. Each flaky event is appended to `.sdd/tdd.jsonl` as `{type:"flaky",check,retry,policy,outcome}`. Retries reporting only skipped/todo/xfail tests, zero tests, or no assertions cannot recover the failure or append flaky evidence (#335); remaining retries may still recover with an executed pass. A consistent failure stays a plain failure. Write deterministic tests: no fixed `sleep`, injected clock/random, port 0, generous timeouts, isolate signal/kill tests.
- `prepare: {cmd, outputs?, inputs?, timeoutMs?}` in config (auto-set from the `build` script by `init`): `gate` runs it before checks and caches by input hash (`.sdd/prepare-cache.json`); skipped when inputs and `outputs` are unchanged. `gate --changed` snapshots changed paths before preparation, so a preparation command that normalizes a lockfile cannot remove its workspace members or transitive consumers from check scope.
- Gate input integrity (#342): both full and changed gates hash annotated files, specs/approval artifacts, the ledger, policy/config inputs, protected oracle data and known check definitions before running commands. Direct prepare/check wrapper files and their local imports use the same protected closure. Each prepare, check, scoped fallback and retry is checked immediately afterward; mutation, deletion or added specs/annotated files fails regardless of `scopePolicy`, and remaining commands are not run. Mutating preparation is not cached. Declared `prepare.outputs` can regenerate oracle/artifact outputs, but cannot exempt annotated files, specs, the ledger, policy inputs or command definitions. Ordinary generated build outputs and gate-owned flaky ledger appends remain supported. These are command-boundary integrity checks, not a sandbox: a command that mutates and restores an input entirely within its execution is not detected.

- `.sdd/tdd.jsonl` is append-only (#328, #346): `gate` and `tdd check` FAIL if a baseline (HEAD / `--baseline <ref>` for gate) entry was removed or modified. A missing file counts as removal of every baseline entry, even in `gate --changed` with no in-scope REQs. A never-committed or empty baseline ledger is not a regression; appends and `tdd merge-ledger` remain allowed.
- Tracker r32 (#347): committed-ledger comparisons capture up to 64 MB with a 60-second timeout. Larger captures, read failures, signals and invalid baseline refs FAIL closed; partial output is never compared or treated as no history. Only a verified absent baseline ledger, unborn HEAD or non-Git project skips the comparison.
- Ledger integrity (#345) includes event semantics, not just hashes: version 1, contiguous sequence numbers, valid nondecreasing timestamps (equal times allowed), and required fields for each event type. Green/Refactor require `exit: 0`; a passing Red needs an explicit nonempty `characterization` or `retest` reason, not just `weak: true`. Invalid events fail both gate modes and `tdd check` and cannot supply evidence. For a whole-file runner whose selected test observably passes while a sibling fails, `exit` records the selected outcome (0), and `runnerExit` preserves the nonzero process status.

## Test runners per stack
- Go/Rust: default `testCmd` is `go test ./... -run '{IDU}(_|$)'` (e.g. `TEST_CALC_001`, name test funcs `TestTEST_CALC_001_…`) / `cargo test {idu}` (`test_calc_001_…`). Placeholders: `{id}`, `{idu}` (complete annotated function/method when resolvable), `{IDU}` (UPPER_SNAKE). Direct Cargo commands resolve the full module-qualified name and add `-- --exact`. Go and Rust were verified end-to-end (Red/Green/gate). Rust inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests protect their test regions and shared test helpers/data, excluding annotated production code. Go `[build failed]` is a load error, not a Red.
- Maven / Gradle (`./gradlew` if present) / CMake+CTest are auto-detected (verified: Maven 3.9 + JUnit5, Gradle 8.14 + JUnit5, CMake/ctest). Name the test method / ctest test so it contains the lowercase ID (`test_calc_001_add` for `TEST-CALC-001`); `{idu}` is substituted into `-Dtest=*#*{idu}*`, `--tests *{idu}*` and `ctest -R`. Gradle runs through a temporary init script (`failOnNoMatchingTests=false` + a `Tests run: N` total per task), so multi-project builds work from the root and a subproject without a match does not fail the build; multi-module Maven works from the root too (zero-test modules are ignored when another module ran tests). Maven `gate --changed` runs `-pl <changed modules> -amd` (dependents included; falls back to the full check when changes are outside any module); Gradle `--changed` runs the full check. POM/Gradle build-script errors are load errors, not Red. Gradle 8 needs JDK ≤ 24 (set `JAVA_HOME`). CMake builds into `build/` (git-ignore it); it configures once, builds incrementally with the log shown only on failure, and `--changed` runs the full (incremental) check.
- Makefile (`make test TEST={idu}` — your `test` target must pass `$(TEST)` to the runner to filter; verified with a C runner) and .NET (`*.sln`/`*.slnx`/`*.csproj` → `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~{idu}`; verified with xUnit: `tdd red/green/refactor`, `gate`, `gate --changed`) are auto-detected after the language-specific stacks. In a nested layout only csproj files referencing `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` (or `<IsTestProject>true`) become `projects`; test-less class libraries do not. xUnit, NUnit and MSTest all work through the VSTest filter (`FullyQualifiedName~{idu}`); `{idu}` is the lowercase ID when the file contains it, else the method name below `@id` (`[Fact]`/`[Test]`/`[TestCase(..)]`/`[TestMethod]`/`[DataRow(..)]` lines are skipped; `[TestCase]`/`[DataRow]` rows run as one test). `bin/` and `obj/` next to a project file are never scanned for `@id`, even without `.gitignore`. Within one sdd process (a batch `tdd red A B C`, or several checks on the same target) a repeat `dotnet test` gets `--no-build` only when the previous run built cleanly (no `error CS/MSB/NETSDK/NU`) and no tracked file (other than `.sdd/`) changed since; a changed tree, a failed build or a different target always rebuilds, and single runs always build. The default .NET check has `changedCmd` `sh -c 'for p in "$@"; do dotnet test "$p" --nologo || r=1; done; exit $r' sdd {changedTestProjects}`: `{changedTestProjects}` = changed test projects plus test projects that (transitively) `ProjectReference` a changed project (csproj / `Directory.Build.props` references, owner = nearest csproj of a changed file). A changed `.sln`/`.slnx`/`Directory.Build.*`/`Directory.Packages.props`/`global.json`/`nuget.config`, or no changed file inside a project, prints `cannot scope changes for {changedTestProjects} — running the full check`. In a nested layout the test project's `dependsOn` is derived from its `ProjectReference`s (and shared props above it). `tdd stub` supports C# (see references/stubs.md); the default `changedTimeoutMs` is 60 s, raise it for slow builds. Weak-Red detection attributes a name-less `NotImplementedException` via the first stack frame.
- Test-name fallback: if the test file does not contain the lowercase ID, `{idu}` becomes the name of the test declared right below `@id` (skipping annotations/comments), so camelCase JUnit methods (`void addsNumbers()`) work without renaming. Keep the `@id` comment directly above the test.
- PHP (`composer.json`/`phpunit.xml` → `phpunit --do-not-cache-result --filter {idu} {file}`, `vendor/bin/phpunit` if present; PHPUnit 13.4+ uses `--do-not-record-test-run-history` instead, detected with `--version` for both TDD and checks), Julia (`Project.toml` → `julia --project=. {file}`, whole file per run); the default `gate` check is `Pkg.test()`, which needs a package registry even for stdlib test deps — when it fails with a registry/network error and `test/runtests.jl` exists the check prints `INFRA: ...` and falls back to `julia --project=. test/runtests.jl` and R (`DESCRIPTION` → `testthat::test_file`, whole file per run; verified with testthat 3; set `R_LIBS_USER` if testthat is in a user library) are auto-detected. Name PHP test methods so they contain the lowercase ID. Existing configs are not rewritten: override both PHPUnit commands when upgrading.
- Other stacks (C/C++/Java/…, verified with plain `sh run_tests.sh <name-filter>` runners): `init` warns that testCmd is a Node fallback; set `testCmd` yourself to a runner that takes the test-name filter, e.g. `["sh","run_tests.sh","{idu}"]` (the runner must exit non-zero when no test matches), and a `checks` entry for the full suite. Annotate with `//` or `/* */` comments; `.c .h .cc .cpp .cxx .hpp .hh .java` are scanned.
- `init` re-run keeps an existing config (delete it to re-detect).

## Monorepos
- Go module boundaries are independent: `init` registers every nested `go.mod`, even with a root Go module or another enclosing nested module, and retains the root checks. `go test ./...` does not check nested modules (#161). Delete an existing config and re-run `init` to opt into this detection.
- For direct Go `testCmd`, `tdd` adds verbose reporting and replaces `-run` with the exact annotated function or literal `t.Run` hierarchy (regex metacharacters escaped). `-json` is supported for target verdicts and diagnostics. A parent/package failure alone is not the subtest's Red (#161–#162).
- With a nested `--root`, `gate --changed` converts Git paths to that root, ignores changes outside it, and checks affected evidence/projects; quoted paths and renames are supported. `gate --changed --baseline <ref>` also scopes everything committed since `<ref>`; a changed non-code `artifacts` file puts its consumers' REQs in scope (#254).
- Polyglot monorepo: when the repo root has no manifest, `init` finds nested manifests (go.mod, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, pom.xml, …) and writes `projects: [{root, testCmd, checks}]`. `tdd` runs a test with its project's `testCmd` in that directory (`{file}` is relative to it); `gate` runs every project's checks as `<root>:<name>` in its cwd; `gate --changed` skips projects with no changed files.
- Mixed monorepo: if the root has a manifest (e.g. package.json), nested projects of a *different* stack (services/go) are still added to `projects`; nested projects of the same stack (npm workspaces) stay with the root. `projects[].dependsOn: ["libs/shared"]` (manual) makes `gate --changed` run the project when a dependency root changes; the path may be any shared directory (e.g. `contract/` shared by a TS API and a Python worker), and `gate --changed` hints when root-owned files changed that no project depends on. Root checks (no `cwd`) are skipped when every changed file is inside a nested project. A project check with `changedCmd`/`hubFallbackCmd` gets `{changedFiles}`/`{changedTests}`/`{changedScopes}` relative to the project root; a dependency-only change runs the full project check. `dependsOn` is transitive (a project that depends on another project's root also inherits that project's `dependsOn`, #241). `projects[].dependsOnMode: "referenced"` (#287) makes `impact` on a shared data file reach that project only when one of its files names the file's path or basename; the default (`declared`) keeps the over-approximation and lists such projects on a `declared dependsOn only` line. `artifacts: {"contract/x.json": ["src/a.ts"]}` declares files depending on a non-code artifact so `impact` traverses it (#242); in `gate --changed` a changed artifact also runs the project holding one of its consumers (#308). A declared artifact missing from disk fails `gate` and `gate --changed` (#320).
- Filters are token-anchored (#141): default node/vitest/jest patterns are `{id}(?![0-9A-Za-z])` (TEST-S-001 does not select TEST-S-0011); Maven/Gradle use a suffix match (`*#*{idu}`, `*{idu}`). `{idu}` keeps the case the name has in the test file (NUnit/xUnit `FullyQualifiedName~` is case-sensitive).
- Runtime exact selection (#164) refines the stored placeholder commands: CTest uses an anchored full function-name regex; PHPUnit uses `/::<method>(?:\s+with data set .*)?$/`; .NET uses `FullyQualifiedName=<namespace>.<class>.<method>` when the qualified declaration is resolvable, plus normal-verbosity console results. Parsed outcomes belong to the exact target, not a longer sibling.
- Git is optional (#163): nested manifest/project discovery, import graphs and C# stubs fall back to filesystem discovery. `gate --changed` cannot infer an empty diff from unavailable Git; it reports the unavailable scope and runs a full gate.
- Gradle generated init scripts live under the project's `.sdd/`, are removed after the command, and report `Tests run`, `Failures` and `Skipped` for TDD, full checks and scoped checks (#165). Disabled/skipped-only Gradle/CTest/Julia full checks are INCOMPLETE, not PASS; mixed executed/skipped runs remain valid.
- Exact ownership refinements (#171–#180): Cargo also selects the owning package and executable (including out-of-line unit modules); Maven/Gradle selectors use the fully qualified class/method. Gradle emits per-test identities and Java XML reports are refreshed before TDD attribution. Default CTest selection discovers a unique method/ID registration rather than assuming the C function name is the registration. PHPUnit dataset patterns span newlines. .NET custom `TestName`/`DisplayName` cases retain method identity; skipped-only normal/minimal VSTest checks are INCOMPLETE. Direct `julia --project=. {file}` runners enable verbose nested summaries without source edits; custom Julia runners must provide observable target summaries.
- Batch-3 refinements (#181–#188): local Rust test modules/data and C/C++ oracle includes participate in evidence hashes transitively (annotated production is excluded; other local includes are conservatively protected). Rust wildcard imports retain conservative cross-crate impact. Nested Java selectors use `$`; nested C# classes/records use `+`, and direct .NET TDD scopes to the owning csproj. Maven/Gradle must expose fresh target results; overloaded JUnit method names are refused, so give each test a unique name within its class. Inline JUnit annotations and PHPUnit lifecycle attributes/aliases participate in isolated hashes. CTest registration ID delimiters may be punctuation or underscores; names are selected uniquely, escaped and anchored, and standard assertions in reachable C helpers count as Red without treating unrelated signals as evidence.
- Julia custom runners: `["julia","--compile=min","--project=.","test/runner.jl","{file}"]` preserves the launcher's `ARGS[1]`; automatic `-e` verbosity injection applies only when `{file}` is the actual executed script operand. Custom `AbstractTestSet` types are not given new constructor keywords and must print target summaries. Complete hyphenated IDs are matched exactly; `--expect` searches only target failure blocks. Explained `--retest` accepts an executed passing changed target as weak Red even when a sibling fails.
- Wave-2a (#189–#198): local support/oracle closure now includes Rust raw/concat manifest paths, nested path modules, bare angle headers, local Java/PHP/C# inherited support and Julia includes. Composed/qualified/aliased/multiline lifecycle declarations respect class ownership. Default PHPUnit filters are class-qualified; direct .NET TDD adds a fresh TRX logger under `.sdd/results/` and aggregates every row selected by the exact method filter. Generic fixtures use bounded selection plus mandatory runtime method metadata rather than an impossible nongeneric equality. CTest whitespace names and C++ pretty-function assertions retain attribution. Qualified standard Julia macro/type spellings get nested-summary verbosity too.
- Wave-2b (#199–#205): Cargo `include!` tests retain enclosing modules and require explicit `--lib`/`--bin NAME`/`--test NAME`/`--example NAME` when shared across targets. C/C++ oracle discovery uses the owning compilation database's include paths, defines and forced includes; unresolved macro inputs are refused. Julia standard `Test` aliases get nested verbosity; generic NUnit TRX method names accept argument rows but not longer siblings. Generated production ownership and handwritten annotation timing are detailed in `stubs.md`.
- **Elixir / ExUnit** (`mix.exs` → `mix test {file}`, check `mix test`): TDD rewrites `{file}` to `file:LINE` of the `test "..."` following the `# @id`, so only that test runs and a failing sibling is never attributed to it. Tests are discovered as `test "..."` / `describe "..."` (reported as `test <describe> <name>`) with optional `@tag`; `@id`/`@verifies` live in `#` comments above the test. `N tests, 0 failures` with every test excluded/skipped (`@tag :skip`, `--only` filters) is not Green or Red; `** (CompileError)` and `module X is not available` are load errors.
- `generated: ["contract/**"]` (#293): paths/globs of build outputs a test reads; they are dropped from the oracle dependency set (no "oracle dependency changed" refusal, but also no oracle checking of them). `[src: file:line]` provenance in a REQ row is excluded from the row hash, so re-anchoring lines does not invalidate Green. Not yet handled: crate-wide Rust oracle narrowing, conftest.py per-test consistency, drift checks of `[src:]` lines in the gate.
- Wave-15 r21b (#308/#301 decisions): a changed `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` whose workspace `members` live under a project dir runs that project's checks and is not reported as "root-owned data". Not changed (no repro or needs redesign): `--baseline` after a merge (plain `git diff <ref>` already covers merges), scoped-Rust rerun de-duplication, runtime-read contract consumers (declare them via `dependsOn`/`artifacts`), project-granular impact noise.

- `specEditPolicy: "reapprove"` (default unset = warn only): on a T1 feature (no approval lock), `tdd refactor` after the wording of an already-Green REQ row changed is refused unless `--wording "<why the behaviour is unchanged>"` is given (that flag is the re-approval; a behaviour change needs `tdd red` then `tdd green`). Until then `gate` keeps failing with `changed in the spec`. Ledgers and configs without the key behave as before.
- `artifactProducers: {"contract/golden.json": "llcli golden"}` (r26d): a generated artifact (or a producer given as a file path, e.g. `build.rs`) that the test reads is not locked into the Red→Green oracle hash: regenerating it between Red and Green is accepted, the artifact sha is recorded in the ledger (`produced`) and Green prints `generated artifact regenerated since Red`. `impact <artifact>` lists the declared producer. Undeclared, the refusal names this key; the alternative is to commit the regenerated file before Red. Unlike `generated` (#293), the sha is recorded. Weak-Red notes: an assertion-only helper defined in the test file (`near(got(..))`) is not a setup call, and `--expect "<text>"` that matches the failure and says more than the stub's own `not implemented: <name>` message overrides the setup classification.
- `artifactStaleness: true` (#309, opt-in): Green/Refactor entries record `artifactShas` for each config `artifacts` file whose path or basename the test file names; editing such a file stales that test (`artifact <path> changed since last Green/Refactor` → `tdd refactor <id>` or `tdd red <id> --retest "<reason>"` + `tdd green`). Entries without `artifactShas` keep the old behaviour. (#321) A test that reaches a declared consumer file (`artifacts` value) through imports, transitively within the project (JS/TS), also records that artifact, even when it never names it. `artifacts` must be an object `{artifact: [consumers]}`; an array is accepted with a warning (each entry becomes an artifact without consumers).
- `artifactGranularity: "test"` (#312, opt-in, with `artifactStaleness`): a test's artifact hashes consider only its own `@id` lines plus the preamble before the first `@id`, so sibling tests that never name the artifact stay valid (re-record with `tdd refactor` to apply). `tdd refactor --stale` also selects artifact-stale tests. `impact <artifact>` lists only files that name a declared artifact; `impact <Cargo.toml>` reaches the workspace members' REQs (`members` globs like `crates/*` are expanded, also for `gate --changed` project attribution).
- `preambleGranularity: "symbol"` (#300, opt-in): by default a test's evidence covers its own `@id` region plus the whole shared preamble, so editing any helper/fixture stales every test in the file. With `"symbol"` the preamble is split into (a) imports/`use`/includes and other non-definition statements (any change still stales all tests) and (b) top-level helper/fixture definitions (`function`/`class`/`const`/`let`/`type`, Python `def`/`class`/`NAME =`, Rust `fn`/`const`/`static`/`struct`/`enum`/`trait`/`impl`): a change stales only tests whose own body (transitively through other helpers) names that helper. Supported: TS/JS, Python, Rust (Rust `fn` helpers were already scoped); other languages keep the whole-preamble behaviour. Ledgers recorded before enabling still match their old hash while unchanged. With `"symbol"`, the `@implements` block of a Rust `struct`/`enum` also covers that type's `impl` blocks (`impl X`, `impl Trait for X`). `tdd refactor --stale` selects exactly the tests the gate says to re-run with `tdd refactor`, and when none is selected it names any annotated file edited outside every CODE span (with its tests) instead of staying silent (#317).
- Scope confidence (r24a, design 3.1): `gate --changed` records each run check as `exact` (scoped, or a project whose files changed) or `widened` (full run because the change could not be scoped) and prints `scope: exact=N widened=N unknown=N` (`--json` adds a `scope` object). `unknown` = changed files no project root, `dependsOn`, `artifacts`, or root check claims. `scopePolicy: "warn"` (default when the key is absent) warns with the file list; `"strict"` fails (`init` writes `strict` into NEW configs only). `unscoped: ["misc/**"]` and `--allow-unscoped <glob[,glob]>` waive files (the flag is recorded as a `scope-waiver` ledger entry). Always ignored: `**/*.md`, `.github/**`, `LICENSE`, `.sdd/**` (explicit skip list; extend with `unscoped`). A root check no longer claims `*.sh` files (#316): an unmapped shell script is `unknown` like a `.txt`. A new (untracked/added) source file under a project root with no `@id`/`@implements` warns (`scopePolicy: "strict"` fails) and is listed by `--explain` as `unannotated` (`scope.unannotated` in `--json`); waive with `unscoped`/`--allow-unscoped`. A root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`/`rust-toolchain*`/`.cargo/config*`, JS `package.json`/lockfiles, Python `pyproject.toml`/`requirements*.txt`/lockfiles run the checks of every project of that ecosystem (a project is of an ecosystem when its root holds the manifest). The "no changed files … skipped" messages state the input closure they were computed from.
- r29a (#327): `gate --changed` fixes the changed-file set before running checks (a check that rewrites `Cargo.lock` cannot hide the change from later projects); a lockfile (`Cargo.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`) in a workspace sub-root widens to every project under that dir, like the root-level rule.
- r27c (#322): a root manifest/lockfile change that widens to projects (e.g. `Cargo.toml` → Rust crates) also runs every project that `dependsOn` (transitively) a widened project, so a Python project spawning the rebuilt binary is not SKIPPED; such a dependent with no `checks` of its own is reported as not re-verified and the gate is INCOMPLETE.
- Scope confidence (r24a, design 3.1): `gate --changed` records each run check as `exact` (scoped, or a project whose files changed) or `widened` (full run because the change could not be scoped) and prints `scope: exact=N widened=N unknown=N` (`--json` adds a `scope` object). `unknown` = changed files no project root, `dependsOn`, `artifacts`, or root check claims. `scopePolicy: "warn"` (default when the key is absent) warns with the file list; `"strict"` fails (`init` writes `strict` into NEW configs only). `unscoped: ["misc/**"]` and `--allow-unscoped <glob[,glob]>` waive files (the flag is recorded as a `scope-waiver` ledger entry). Always ignored: `**/*.md`, `.github/**`, `LICENSE`, `.sdd/**` (explicit skip list; extend with `unscoped`). A new (untracked/added) source file under a project root with no `@id`/`@implements` warns (`scopePolicy: "strict"` fails) and is listed by `--explain` as `unannotated` (`scope.unannotated` in `--json`); waive with `unscoped`/`--allow-unscoped`. A root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`/`rust-toolchain*`/`.cargo/config*`, JS `package.json`/lockfiles, Python `pyproject.toml`/`requirements*.txt`/lockfiles run the checks of every project of that ecosystem (a project is of an ecosystem when its root holds the manifest). The "no changed files … skipped" messages state the input closure they were computed from. A changed file that defines what a gate check runs (#324: the `package.json` script named by `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun run <name>` when that script's text changed vs HEAD; `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini` behind a pytest check; a `.cargo/config[.toml]` alias used by a `cargo <alias>` check) warns naming the check and script (`scopePolicy: "strict"` fails); test counts are not compared. The full `gate` (#325) also compares a hash of that check-defining text (script text, `[tool.pytest*]` sections of `pyproject.toml` or the whole `pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`, the cargo alias line) with the one recorded as `checkDefShas` by the last `tdd green`/`refactor`; a difference warns naming the check and file (`scopePolicy: "strict"` fails). Fail-open: no recorded `checkDefShas` (older ledger) = no warning; re-run `tdd refactor` to re-record after a reviewed change.
- New check definitions (#333) are compared too: adding `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, or a Cargo alias cannot bypass the full-gate hash guard by leaving previously recorded files unchanged. Pytest `conftest.py` hooks discovered beneath the check root and in its workspace ancestors are also tracked. Additions, edits and removals warn under `scopePolicy: "warn"` and fail under `"strict"`; review the change before refreshing evidence with `tdd refactor`.
- Check-definition closure (r31a, #340/#343/#344; extends #324/#325/#333): `checkDefShas` now covers literal file references recursively across check `cmd`/`changedCmd`/`hubFallbackCmd`, wrapper/interpreter scripts, nested package scripts, and Makefile recipes. For example, `npm run test` → `node tools/check.mjs` → `sh tools/select.sh` includes both wrappers and the `test`, `pretest`, and `posttest` script definitions (also for pnpm/yarn). Unrelated package-script edits remain silent. Cargo checks cover whole ancestor `.cargo/config{,.toml}` files and `rust-toolchain{,.toml}` files, including ancestors above the repo, plus Cargo-home config. Full and changed gates both compare the closure with the last Green/refactor, including additions/removals and committed drift; changed gates also compare it with `--baseline` (default `HEAD`). `unscoped` does not waive definition drift. Under strict policy, review the diff, run `tdd refactor` to refresh Green hashes, and commit the reviewed files to refresh the Git baseline. Older ledgers without `checkDefShas` still skip the Green comparison. Discovery is conservative and static: literal paths are followed with cycle protection, but dynamic path construction and environment-dependent execution are not comprehensively modeled.

- Config weakening (r28b, #326): `gate --changed` warns when `.sdd/config.json` loosens `scopePolicy`/`specEditPolicy`/`flaky`/`unscoped`/`artifactStaleness`/`artifactGranularity` vs the baseline, and fails if the baseline had `scopePolicy: "strict"` unless `--allow-config-weaken` is passed.
- Config weakening, run/scope keys (r29e, #331): the same guard (and the full gate, against `HEAD`'s config; untracked/unchanged = silent) also reports a project's `checks`/`testCmd`/`changedCmd` removed or replaced by a no-op (`true`, `:`, `echo …`, `exit 0`), fewer checks, removed `dependsOn` edges, removed `artifacts` entries/consumers, new `generated` globs and new `artifactProducers`. Adding projects/checks/consumers is silent. Same severity and `--allow-config-weaken` override.
- Runner selection integrity (r30a, #332): changing arguments of recognized test-runner commands in root/project `testCmd`, `changedCmd` or named checks warns as possible coverage narrowing (for example `cargo test` → `cargo test wire_round_trip`, pytest `-k`/test paths, Node `--test-name-pattern`). Full and changed gates fail when the baseline policy is strict unless acknowledged with `--allow-config-weaken`. This is conservative: widening and operational argument edits also need review; unchanged commands and non-runner command edits do not trigger this diagnostic.
- Runner environment integrity (r31b, #341): TDD commands, `prepare`, root/project checks (including `changedCmd`, full fallbacks and retries), and scope-discovery commands inherit only the allowlist below. Inherited `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`/`PYTEST_PLUGINS`, Cargo flag/target-runner variables, `RUSTFLAGS`/`RUSTDOCFLAGS`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `GOFLAGS`, JVM/Maven/Gradle options, shell startup hooks and custom selector variables are dropped. Each Red/Green/refactor ledger entry and `gate --json` records `runnerEnv: {allowlist, inherited, removed}` containing variable **names only**, never values.
  - Allowed runtime/user locations: `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`; Windows `SYSTEMROOT`, `WINDIR`, `COMSPEC`, `PATHEXT`, `USERPROFILE`, `HOMEDRIVE`, `HOMEPATH`, `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `PROGRAMFILES`, `PROGRAMFILES(X86)`, `PROGRAMDATA`.
  - Allowed tool locations: `JAVA_HOME`, `JDK_HOME`, `DOTNET_ROOT`, `DOTNET_ROOT_X64`, `DOTNET_ROOT_X86`, `DOTNET_CLI_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `CARGO_HOME`.
  - Allowed locale/presentation: `TZ`, `LANG`, `LANGUAGE`, `LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE`, `LC_COLLATE`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LC_NUMERIC`, `LC_TIME`, `LC_MONETARY`, `CI`, `TERM`, `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`. Names are matched case-insensitively.
  - Required extra variables must be explicit in the configured command, e.g. `["env","SERVICE_URL=...","python3","-m","pytest"]`. Explicit assignments are preserved, not silently stripped. Changes to recognized runners behind `env` (including `-i`, `-u`, `-C`, `-S`, long equivalents and `--`) or shell assignments now count as runner-selection changes under the existing strict/warn policy and `--allow-config-weaken` acknowledgement. Nested env/shell prefixes and quoted assignment values are recognized.
  - This closes inherited runner options, not arbitrary execution: commands, wrappers, executable lookup and configuration beneath allowed home/tool directories remain trusted. Options affecting the initial `node sdd.mjs` process itself must be cleared by its caller.
- Tracker r33 (#353, #354): Cargo compiler wrappers (`rustc-wrapper` / `rustc-workspace-wrapper`, config/environment/`--config`) are execution definitions even when annotated or compiled; snapshots fingerprint raw binary bytes and follow literal wrapper inputs. Node checks fingerprint package resolution metadata (`imports`, `exports`, `type`, `main`, `name`), including nested package boundaries and installed package metadata, without hashing unrelated scripts. Compiler/resolution changes between Red and Green require a fresh assertion Red; legacy Red records remain readable. Changed Cargo project checks verify their own annotated surface, not deliberately skipped sibling projects; full-gate and checked-project executed-test verification remain mandatory.
- Tracker r33 (#355, #356): Node spec/TAP gate checks require executed annotated TEST IDs in the selected file/project surface; skipped/TODO targets cannot borrow a passing sibling, including on flaky retries. Unannotated skips remain valid. Explicit name filters retain command/config provenance review. Pytest plugin declarations must use literal module-name strings, lists or tuples (multiline/comments allowed); computed names, concatenation, calls and augmented assignments fail closed before TDD execution or evidence writes, regardless of scope policy. Literal local plugins and their transitive imports remain definition inputs.
